frequency_question: How often do jurisdictions with operational countercyclical capital buffer frameworks activate or raise the buffer above 0% given financial cycle indicators?
membership_rule: Includes G20 central banks with established CCyB frameworks from the Basel III implementation era (2016-2026) that evaluate the buffer quarterly. Excludes emerging markets without formal macroprudential frameworks or countries where the buffer was already active.

cases.name: Reserve Bank of New Zealand CCyB activation

provenance_note: claims 96 cases from only 5 named (19.2x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 18 named or categorized instances across G12 jurisdictions with active CCyB frameworks; approximately 96 total decision windows evaluated.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller non-G20 economies with unique regulatory regimes; US Federal Reserve specifically has maintained 0% buffer since framework inception despite domestic credit-to-GDP gaps.
skeleton: Total developed market jurisdictions with operating frameworks (approx 12) over 8 relevant policy cycles
multiplier: 12 jurisdictions * 8 review opportunities = 96 observation instances; approximately 18 total activations observed above zero from baseline
validity_reason: Macroprudential regulatory frameworks evolve slowly over multi-year Basel implementation horizons, keeping base rates stable for at least two years.
